title: The Cardinal C for Flipping Arguments
description: Define the Cardinal combinator C = lambda f: lambda a: lambda b: f(b)(a) to flip argument order and derive it from S, B, and K.

steps.description: Define K, S, B, the Cardinal C = lambda f: lambda a: lambda b: f(b)(a), and curried subtraction subtract = lambda x: lambda y: x - y.

steps.question: Why does subtract_10(3) compute 3 - 10 = -7 instead of 10 - 3 = 7?
steps.answer: Because C(subtract)(10)(3) flips the two arguments a=10 and b=3, calling subtract(3)(10).

steps.description: Partially apply 10 into the second slot using C(subtract)(10) and call subtract_10(3) to print -7.
Construct C_from_SK = S(B(B)(S))(K(K)) and verify that C_from_SK(subtract)(10)(3) also prints -7.
Step into subtract_10(3) to see C pass b=3 first and a=10 second into subtract.
